tasks.intent: General time integrator: integrate valid signal values over elapsed time
tasks.requires: Signal definition, unit, validity and the intended actual/fixed/DBC interval rule. The minimal example uses actual elapsed time.
tasks.applicable: Use calculations[].operation: integral for time integration, including unequal timestamps and held values. The selected interval rule determines the time weight.
tasks.not_applicable: Do not substitute FAST_MESSAGE_ENERGY just because the result is energy. Fast requires all formula inputs in the current message and a defined contribution for each matching message.
tasks.check: After run, locate the session CSV in the completion manifest outputs: energy（J） is 30 and energy：状态 is 完整. This single ASC with concatenate is read in the current process although the configured upper limit is 4.
tasks.verify:
python -m chronaxis validate ../../Current/examples/calculation-minimal.yaml --format json
python -m chronaxis run ../../Current/examples/calculation-minimal.yaml --output result-general-time-integral

tasks.intent: Read and decode several files from one continuous charge in parallel

tasks.verify:
python -m chronaxis validate ../../Current/examples/continuous-parallel.yaml --format json
python -m chronaxis run ../../Current/examples/continuous-parallel.yaml --output result-continuous-files

tasks.intent: Continuous BLF/ASC volumes: require multiple conditions for longer than a threshold, then integrate energy over the full qualifying interval in kWh
tasks.requires: Raw ASC/BLF and matching DBC; target signals, codes, units, comparisons, continuous duration, and integration scope. Do not require types, units, or periods to be repeated when the DBC supplies them.
tasks.applicable: Custom state and numeric conditions; inclusive or strict duration thresholds; integration from condition onset; optional energy unit. The example uses strict >60s, default onset, and actual elapsed time.
tasks.not_applicable: For per-message contributions query MESSAGE_ENERGY; choose FAST_MESSAGE_ENERGY only when its current-message restrictions fit. Independent tasks use BATCH; fast template totals use FAST_TEMPLATE_TOTAL.
tasks.alternative: charge_session applies only to its strict current > comparison, duration >= comparison, Wh/Ah outputs, and direction/measurement-point requirements. Do not choose it merely because a task mentions charging.
tasks.check: After run succeeds, open the path in the CLI JSON manifest field and use outputs to locate the named readable tables. The event table has one qualifying interval: the same row has 开始时间（s）=61, 结束时间（s）=122, energy_kwh（kWh）=0.06777777777777777, energy_kwh：状态=完整 (complete), and an empty energy_kwh：说明. Exactly 60 seconds produces no event; do not replace strict comparison with 60.1 seconds. No ID join is needed for the default readable CSV.
tasks.verify:
python -m chronaxis validate ../../Current/examples/conditional-energy.yaml --format json
python -m chronaxis run ../../Current/examples/conditional-energy.yaml --output result-condition-energy

tasks.intent: Charging activities, electric charge, and charging energy
tasks.requires: Mode codes, positive current direction, terminal measurement point, voltage, thresholds, and duration. The teaching example uses ASC; for BLF replace the logs, DBC, and bindings with your own.
tasks.check: After run succeeds, open the path in the CLI JSON manifest field and use outputs to locate the named readable tables. The event row starts at 1 s and ends at 3 s, with demo_preset_energy（Wh）=2.2222222222222223 and demo_preset_charge（Ah）=0.005555555555555556, both complete. Check applicability first: current equals current_min is excluded, duration equals minimum_duration qualifies, and onset is the default integration start.
tasks.verify:
python -m chronaxis validate ../../Current/examples/preset-charge-energy.yaml --format json
python -m chronaxis run ../../Current/examples/preset-charge-energy.yaml --output result-charge
tasks.applicable: Mode equals the specified integer code and current is strictly greater than current_min. After reaching minimum_duration, calculate from condition onset. Outputs are Wh for energy and Ah for electric charge. Positive current means charging, and the measurement point is the battery-pack terminal.
tasks.not_applicable: Do not directly apply charge_session when the task needs current >= threshold, a strict duration threshold, direct kWh output, another state combination, or unconfirmed preset direction/measurement-point requirements.
tasks.alternative: Use CONDITION_ENERGY and ../../Current/examples/conditional-energy.yaml with an ordinary condition_duration rule and event-scope integral. Preserve the comparisons, duration comparison, and output unit. Ordinary U*I integration needs no extra direction/measurement-point metadata or 95% coverage threshold.
